meta.principle: This session publishes decision RULES with sourced inputs and a transparent cost stack. It does not publish a property value, a rent, or a dollar ranking, because those inputs are unknown. Any workbook on this repository that does is flagged, not endorsed.
meta.illustrative_price_note: The $4,000,000 figure used in the cost stack is a DEMONSTRATION PRICE, chosen by this session so the arithmetic can be checked and re-run at any price. It is not a valuation, not an asking price, not an appraisal, and it is not derived from any property data. Every percentage and fixed input in the stack is sourced.

cost_stack.description: Transaction and tax cost of an outright sale, at the demonstration price, inside the City of Los Angeles, for a long-held depreciated asset.

inputs.label: Gross sale price (demonstration)
inputs.note: Demonstration only. Replace with a real offer.

inputs.label: City of Los Angeles real property transfer base tax
inputs.note: $2.25 per $500, rounded up to the nearest $500.

inputs.label: County documentary transfer tax (special-city basis)
inputs.note: The page states $0.55 per $500 countywide but the full $1.10 per $1,000 for the five special cities including Los Angeles. The higher of the two published statements is used; the ambiguity is flagged.

inputs.label: Measure ULA special transfer tax
inputs.note: Zero here only because $4.0M is below the $5.4M lower threshold for closings after 2026-06-30. At $5.4M exactly it still does not apply; above it, 4% applies to the whole consideration up to $10.9M, and 5.5% at or above $10.9M. This single line is why the sale decision is jurisdiction-sensitive.

inputs.label: Federal unrecaptured section 1250 recapture
inputs.note: Applies only to the depreciation actually taken. The amount is an owner fact and is blank here; the ceiling rate is official.

inputs.label: Federal long-term capital gain
inputs.note: Plus 3.8% net investment income tax where the statutory thresholds are exceeded.

inputs.label: Net investment income tax
inputs.note: Applies to the lesser of net investment income or MAGI above threshold; whether it bites is an owner fact.

inputs.label: California personal income tax on the gain
inputs.basis: official rule plus official top rate
inputs.unit: percent, top marginal, as ordinary income
inputs.note: California has no preferential capital gains rate (S07); the top marginal rate is 12.30% (S06). The relevant marginal rate depends on the owner's other income and is therefore not asserted here beyond the ceiling.

inputs.label: Brokerage and closing costs
inputs.note: Deliberately blank. No official source publishes a commission or closing-cost schedule; quoting one would be an invented number. Obtain a real listing agreement.

cost_stack.max_statutory_tax_load_note: 25% federal recapture + 20% federal capital gain + 3.8% net investment income tax + 12.30% California, on the applicable components, is the ceiling the sources support (S09, S10, S06, S07). It is a ceiling from four separate rules, not a single published total, and it is not applied as a flat rate to the whole gain.

decisions.name: Sell now, outright, no exchange
decisions.viable_when: You need liquidity or diversification more than you need deferral, or the implied cap rate on a real offer is below the return you can genuinely earn elsewhere after tax.
decisions.benefits: Converts an illiquid, single-tenant, single-city asset into cash; ends seismic, fire, insurance, vacancy and tenant-credit exposure on this asset; removes the renewal negotiation entirely.
decisions.costs: The largest tax bill of any branch: recapture plus federal gain plus net investment income tax plus California at ordinary rates; plus ULA if inside the city and above $5.4M; plus transfer taxes and closing costs.
decisions.principal_risk: Selling into a thin market and paying a peak tax rate to do it.
decisions.risk_level: High, on cost rather than on uncertainty
decisions.verdict: Legitimate, but normally the wrong first move solely because of the tax stack. Justified when liquidity or concentration dominates.

decisions.name: Extend the lease, then sell with long remaining term
decisions.viable_when: The tenant will sign a market-supported extension on acceptable terms, and the added term raises the price by more than the rent concession costs.
decisions.benefits: Attacks the two things that most reduce price, namely short term and rollover risk, without a taxable event. A longer lease widens the buyer pool and improves financeability. Preserves the deferral option for later.
decisions.costs: Any concession you give, the time to negotiate it, and the risk that the tenant's credit deteriorates during the new term.
decisions.principal_risk: Paying for term with rent you cannot recover, or discovering the tenant will not sign at any price you can accept.
decisions.risk_level: Moderate: bounded by the terms actually signed
decisions.verdict: The strongest structural move in most scenarios, and it does not foreclose either of the other two. Fix the lease first, then price the asset.

decisions.name: Extend and hold for income
decisions.viable_when: Renewal rent clears the debt service and reserve with real coverage, the owner can absorb a long vacancy and an insurance shock, and the concentration is acceptable to the owner's overall balance sheet.
decisions.benefits: Keeps the income and the land. Defers all capital gains and preserves a low Proposition 13 basis. No transaction costs. Retains any long-run location upside.
decisions.costs: Continues undiversified exposure to one building, one tenant and one seismic region. Defers, rather than avoids, the eventual tax. Requires capital reserves for roof, structure and systems.
decisions.principal_risk: A correlated local event that removes income and collateral simultaneously, with no second asset to absorb it.
decisions.risk_level: High on tail exposure, low on transaction cost
decisions.verdict: Defensible for an owner whose other assets already provide diversification, and whose reserve can survive two years of vacancy. Not defensible as a default.

decisions.name: Sell and complete a section 1031 exchange
decisions.viable_when: There is real gain to defer, a credible replacement property or several can be identified within 45 days, and financing for the replacement is arranged before the relinquished sale closes.
decisions.benefits: Defers both federal and California gain where the rules are met. Can replace one asset with several, which is the only branch here that directly reduces concentration without a tax cost.
decisions.costs: Execution risk on a fixed 45/180-day clock; intermediary risk; replacement quality risk; possible boot and partial recognition; borrowed debt must generally be replaced.
decisions.principal_risk: Missing the window and paying the full tax anyway, having also paid the transaction costs.
decisions.risk_level: Moderate to high, concentrated in execution
decisions.verdict: The structurally correct exit if the objective is wealth preservation plus diversification. It is a process, not a product, and it needs a named intermediary and identified candidates before listing.

decisions.name: Hold without extending, then decide
decisions.viable_when: Near-term income is needed and no good offer exists, and a dated review trigger is set in advance.
decisions.benefits: No transaction cost now. Keeps optionality while the market or the tenant situation clarifies.
decisions.costs: The remaining term shortens every month, and price falls with it. Doing nothing is itself a decision, and it is the one that most reliably destroys value.
decisions.principal_risk: Drift. Ending up in the final two years of term with no lease, no offer and no exchange plan.
decisions.risk_level: High, because the cost is quiet
decisions.verdict: Acceptable only with a written decision date tied to the actual expiry, and only if that date is before the term becomes short. Never as an unstated default.

decisions.name: Refinance and hold
decisions.viable_when: Existing debt terms are poor, the lease has enough term to support new financing, and coverage survives a stress case.
decisions.benefits: Can release liquidity or lower the coupon without a taxable sale, and without giving up the asset.
decisions.costs: Adds leverage and maturity risk, and does nothing about tenant or location concentration. A refinance into a loan that matures near the lease expiry creates a simultaneous double deadline.
decisions.principal_risk: A maturity wall that coincides with a vacancy or a rate spike.
decisions.verdict: A financing decision, not a solution to the sell-or-renew question. Only after the lease question is settled and the stress case passes.

decision_rule.statement: Fix the lease before pricing the asset, and settle jurisdiction before costing the sale.

gates.question: Is the building inside the City of Los Angeles?
gates.why: Measure ULA applies only inside the city. The difference at a $6M sale is $240,000 of tax. The county documentary transfer tax basis also differs.
gates.action: Confirm with the city planning parcel tool and the recorded deed. This is a yes/no question that changes the answer materially.

gates.question: What is the exact expiry, are the options unilateral or mutual, is there a guaranty, and what are the escalations?
gates.why: Every branch above turns on these five facts, and none of them is public.
gates.action: Read the lease and all amendments. Diarise every notice date backwards from expiry.

gates.question: Who is the obligor, and can they pay through a downturn?
gates.why: The public parent's balance sheet is not the obligor's. Treat the franchisor's own risk factors as a warning about the system, not a credit opinion on this store.
gates.action: Obtain the operating entity's financials, the guaranty and 24 months of rent payment history.

gates.question: What is the after-tax, after-cost number on a real offer?
gates.why: The tax stack, not the headline price, decides whether a sale beats holding. California taxes the gain as ordinary income.
gates.action: Compute with the actual basis and depreciation schedule. Get the ULA and transfer tax computed on the actual price and jurisdiction.

gates.question: What are the parcel's FHSZ class, flood zone, seismic zone and retrofit status, and what does insurance cost and cover?
gates.why: These determine both the reserve required to hold and the discount a buyer will apply.
gates.action: Look up each parcel-level designation and obtain the policy. Do not accept a city-level answer to a parcel-level question.

gates.question: Is there a named intermediary and at least one identified replacement before listing?
gates.why: The 45-day clock starts at closing. Improvising after the fact is how exchanges fail.
gates.action: Engage the intermediary and shortlist replacement assets before signing a listing agreement.

gates.question: What is the date on which this is decided, in writing?
gates.why: Term decays continuously and the cost is invisible until it is large.
gates.action: Set the date at least three years before the actual expiry. Put it in the calendar with an owner, not a topic.
